html: That hot, sour feeling rising behind the breastbone happens when stomach acid splashes up into the food pipe (esophagus). An occasional episode is common and usually nothing serious.

• Big portions, especially close to bedtime
  • Rich, greasy or spicy dishes
  • Coffee, alcohol and fizzy drinks
  • Bending over or lying flat right after eating

• Eat smaller meals and stop eating two to three hours before bed
  • Raise the head of your bed a few inches
  • Loosen tight waistbands and belts

Chest pressure comes with shortness of breath, sweating, or an ache spreading into an arm or the jaw. Call 911: these can be signs of a heart attack. Also see a clinician if heartburn shows up most weeks or swallowing becomes difficult.

title: Heartburn
abstract: What causes that burning feeling after meals, and the changes that usually help.
